newsitem.title: CHINA: Joyce sees operating profit in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Joyce sees operating profit in 1997/98.

text.p: Joyce Boutique Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it expects to return to operating profitability and achieve higher turnover growth in financial year 1997/98.
"The group expects improved results from operations in Hong Kong and other markets, with the exception of of Thailand, in 1997/98 and 1998/99," the fashion retailer said in a statement.

"With additional contributions expected from major new regional fashion franchises, expanding Joyce Cafe operations and cosmetics...we should see higher turnover growth and a return to operating profitability in 1997/98."
Joyce Boutique posted a 62.7 percent decline in net profit for the year ended March 31 to HK$30.21 million.
It had an operating loss of HK$12.36 million.

"Operating losses, in part non-recurring in nature, were due to delays in openings of major new stores and restaurants; losses in Thailand and Taiwan offsetting gains from Hong Kong retail operations and group subsidiaries; unamortised depreciation costs following consolidation of the Kowloon portfolio, a soft Hong Kong market and a shortfall in tourist sales," Joyce Boutique said.
It said demand for the DKNY fashion and accessories label had declined and the group would cease selling Donna Karan and DKNY in all markets except the Philippines.
"The effect on earnings has been more than compensated by contributions from fast-growing new franchises," it added.
It said Joyce Bangkok, which opened in September 1996, made an operating loss of HK$15 million.
"Thailand's current economic crisis has had a profound effect on sales at Joyce's retail operations in Bangkok, and the group is taking steps to stem losses," Joyce Boutique said.
It said its Taiwan operation made an operating loss of HK$8.6 million, a 47 percent improvement on last year, and was expected to show further improvement in 1997/98.
In the Philippines, operations made a slight loss but were expected to show an improvement this financial year while retail operations in Macau and Malaysia were profitable.
